text:
Shakir Mukhamadullin has landed a real job in Edmonton. After starting his NHL career in San Jose, the 24-year-old has played 13 games at 14.5 minutes a night, topping 19 minutes against Calgary on Oct. 28. His one goal came against Utah on Oct. 15, and he has a power-play point.

The results with him on the ice haven't kept pace with the trust. At five on five, the Oilers get 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) when he plays, about 10 points worse than when he sits. Some of that is cold finishing around him: the team has scored 1.3 fewer goals than its chances deserved with him out there.

There's a case for patience. Evolving-Hockey had him around the middle of the league's defensemen last season (99th of 215), mostly on defensive value, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him moving the puck out with possession on 53% of his exits, over a small nine-game sample. He has a heavy shot too, 93 mph at the top (83rd percentile). The 6-foot-5 former Devils first-rounder needs his on-ice numbers to come up before his minutes come down.
headline: Mukhamadullin's minutes are outrunning his results
